guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 for third-party access on behalf of a user. For read-only issue titles across projects the connected person can access, read_api is the documented least-privilege scope that covers the project issues list endpoint, and it includes pagination. Registration, redirect configuration and token exchange are setup requirements. Customer distribution policy remains unknown.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, including paginated results. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth 2 authorization code with PKCE is documented for server and client apps
findings.detail: GitLab documents the authorization code flow with PKCE as the most secure option and recommends it for client and server apps. The application must be registered first in the user's account settings.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect individually with their own GitLab accounts

evidence.quote: Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) :
This flow is recommended for both client and server apps.
registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API including projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It is a broad read scope, so the integration is limited to read calls only, and the app must not call create, update or delete issue endpoints. The project issues list endpoint is documented as a list call for a specified project, and a private project requires credentials.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing issues in a project the connected person can access

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
List all project issues
If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.

findings.title: Register a user-owned application and store client credentials
findings.detail: A user-owned application requires a name, redirect URI and selected scopes. GitLab then provides an application ID and client secret that the client must store securely.
findings.appliesWhen: Setting up the OAuth app for individual customer accounts

evidence.quote: Create a user-owned application
Enter a Name and Redirect URI .
The OAuth 2 Client ID in the Application ID field.

findings.title: Plan for two-hour access token expiry and refresh-token renewal
findings.detail: By default access tokens expire after two hours, so integrations must use the refresh token to obtain a new access token. Pagination for the issues list uses offset pagination by default with a per_page maximum of 100, and keyset pagination is available for the project issues list.
findings.appliesWhen: Running paginated issue reads over time

evidence.quote: By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations that use access tokens must generate a new token with the refresh_token attribute. Refresh tokens can be used even
Access token expiration History OAuth access token expiry configurable by instance administrators introduced in GitLab 19.1.
per_page Number of items to list per page (default: 20 , max: 100 ).

steps.title: Register a user-owned GitLab OAuth application
steps.detail: Create a user-owned OAuth application in the GitLab account that will connect, with a Name, a Redirect URI and the read_api scope only. GitLab then provides an Application ID (client ID) and Client Secret that must be stored securely. Use the instance origin for GitLab.com or a Self-Managed instance, not a placeholder.
steps.doneWhen: An application exists in Access > Applications with read_api selected, and its Application ID and secret are stored in the app's secret store.

fields: Redirect URI: the URL of the customer app callback, HTTPS in production

steps.detail: Generate STATE, CODE_VERIFIER and CODE_CHALLENGE, then send the connecting person to the authorize endpoint with scope=read_api. This is an unexecuted authorization step for the connecting person to approve in a browser.

REDIRECT_URI: from the app configuration

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code and the CODE_VERIFIER for an access token and refresh token at the token endpoint. This is an unexecuted authorization step; use the documented grant_type and the client_id, code and redirect_uri values.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, refresh_token and expires_in, and the tokens are stored server-side.

fields: RETURNED_CODE: one-time code from the redirect
CODE_VERIFIER: the original random verifier
grant_type: authorization_code (documented constant)

steps.title: Read the first page of project issue titles
steps.detail: Send GET to /api/v4/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/issues?per_page=100 for a project the connected person can access, using the OAuth access token in the Authorization Bearer header. Representative input: a numeric project ID. Expected result: HTTP 200 with a JSON array of issues; read the title of each issue. Private projects require credentials. Boundary check: use GET only; confirm the outgoing request log contains no issue create, update or delete calls and that the token grant is read_api only.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a JSON array of issues with title values, and the Link header is inspected for rel="next". Boundary check: confirm the request log shows only GET requests and no create, update or delete issue calls.

evidence.quote: --header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \
id integer or string Yes The global ID or URL-encoded path of the project .
per_page Number of items to list per page (default: 20 , max: 100 ).

fields: PROJECT_ID: user-provided project ID the connected person can access
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the token exchange response

steps.title: Read the following pages of project issue titles
steps.detail: Take the rel="next" URL from the previous response Link header and request it unchanged with the same Bearer header. If the href is relative, resolve it against the HTTPS instance host only; do not construct a URL or invent a cursor. Collect the title of each issue on every page. Repeat until a response has no rel="next" entry in its Link header, which is the documented end of the listing. Boundary check: use GET only and confirm the request log contains no create, update or delete issue calls.
steps.doneWhen: Every page returns HTTP 200 and the listing ends when the Link header contains no rel="next" entry, with all titles collected. Boundary check: confirm the request log shows only GET requests and no issue create, update or delete calls.

per_page Number of items to list per page (default: 20 , max: 100 ).

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: rel="next" URL from previous response Link header, resolved to HTTPS instance host
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the token exchange response

steps.detail: Confirm the granted scope is read_api and that the app sends no POST, PUT or DELETE to issue endpoints. Inspect the outgoing request log for the issue reads; do not attempt a write to test this.
steps.doneWhen: Logs show only GET requests to issue endpoints and the granted scope is read_api.
